classification.difficultyReason: Eliminate time using the supplied equations, apply the taught identity and solve a factorable quadratic.

content.prompt:
A particle is projected from the origin at $30\text{ m/s}$ and passes through $(30,20)$.

It is given that
$$\underset{\sim}{r}=\begin{pmatrix}30\cos\theta\,t\\-5t^2+30\sin\theta\,t\end{pmatrix}.$$
Show that $\tan^2\theta-6\tan\theta+5=0$ and find both possible angles. Give non-exact angles to $1$ decimal place.

answer.worked:
From the horizontal equation,
$$\begin{align*}30&=30\cos\theta\,t\\t&=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the vertical equation with $y=20$:
$$\begin{align*}20&=30\sin\theta\left(\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\right)-5\left(\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\right)^2\\20&=30\tan\theta-5\sec^2\theta\\20&=30\tan\theta-5(1+\tan^2\theta)\\5\tan^2\theta-30\tan\theta+25&=0\\\tan^2\theta-6\tan\theta+5&=0\\(\tan\theta-1)(\tan\theta-5)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Hence $\tan\theta=1$ or $\tan\theta=5$, giving
$$\theta=45^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad\theta=\tan^{-1}(5)\approx78.7^\circ.$$
